newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks close mixed in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks close mixed in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Indian share prices retreated after early rally to finish mixed on Monday as the absence of foreign funds hurt volumes and kept players on the sidelines, brokers said.
They said the market lacked follow-up support because of a holiday in London and Hong Kong, from where many foreign fund managers operate, but the underlying sentiment was hopeful.
"We're betting on gains this week," said one trader. "The charts also show an upside."
The 30-share benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) ended up 2.15 points at 3,433.55 after rising to 3,460.59.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index lost 4.0 points to 1,009 with the net traded value at 6.37 billion rupees in 34.28 million shares.
The 500-share CRISIL index eased 0.15 points to 686.66.
"The market was directionless," said broker Sunil Kothari. "Activity was very dull. There were few participants and price movements were restricted."
Analysts said expectations the government will make changes to a controversial minimum corporate tax before the proposal is passed by parliament next month was likely to pep up sentiment.
Parliament resumed on Monday after the summer break.
Scootermaker Bajaj Auto gained 4.25 rupees to 1,018.25 buoyed by news that its turnover was up 29 percent at 11.34 billion rupees in the first months of 1996/97 (April-March).
ACC gained 22.50 to 2,121, Ranbaxy 5.25 to 615.25, M&M 3.75 to 352 and TISCO 1.25 to 189.50.
Reliance dropped 4.50 to 209.50 and SBI 1.0 to 266.25.
The Delhi share index fell 1.44 points to 795.80, but DCM Daewoo bucked trend rising 2.50 rupees to 48.
The Madras index gained 6.82 points to 3,588.70 but the Calcutta index shed 1.84 to 445.15. The BSE National index slipped 1.49 points to 1,561.80.
